title: Preeclampsia with Severe Features
scenario: A 29-year-old woman at 34 weeks gestation presents to the obstetric triage unit with a severe frontal headache, blurred vision, and swelling of the face and hands over the past two days.

lines: 29-year-old G1P0 at 34 weeks gestation presents with a 2-day frontal headache unrelieved by acetaminophen, blurred vision with reports of spots, and new facial and hand edema. Reports right upper quadrant discomfort. Fetal movement present. Alert and oriented x3. Deep tendon reflexes 3+ with no clonus at this time.
IV access established. Labs drawn and sent. Continuous fetal monitoring and maternal blood pressure monitoring initiated. Provider notified of elevated blood pressure and symptoms.

Magnesium sulfate loading dose and maintenance infusion started per order. IV labetalol administered for severe-range blood pressure. Client placed in quiet, low-stimulation environment with side rails padded.

Reports headache improving and vision clearer. Blood pressure trending down. Deep tendon reflexes 2+, respirations adequate, urine output 60 mL over the last hour. Fetal heart rate reassuring with moderate variability.
G1P0, 34 weeks gestation by first-trimester dating
No prior history of chronic hypertension or renal disease
Magnesium sulfate 4 g IV loading dose over 20 minutes, then 2 g/hr maintenance infusion
Labetalol 20 mg IV for systolic B/P >= 160 or diastolic >= 110, repeat per protocol
Continuous fetal heart rate and contraction monitoring
Insert indwelling urinary catheter, strict hourly intake and output
Betamethasone 12 mg IM now and in 24 hours
Notify provider for respiratory rate < 12, absent reflexes, or urine output < 30 mL/hr

children.subject: Maternity

options.text: Severe frontal headache unrelieved by acetaminophen

children.rationale: Severe-range blood pressure, a persistent headache, visual disturbances, and right upper quadrant pain are hallmark severe features of preeclampsia and signal risk of eclampsia and organ injury. Fetal movement and vitamin use are expected findings.

children.subject: Maternity
children.stem: For each laboratory finding, click to specify whether it supports HELLP syndrome, worsening preeclampsia, or both. Each finding may support more than one.
children.rationale: HELLP is defined by hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, and low platelets, so thrombocytopenia and elevated AST support it. Rising creatinine and proteinuria reflect worsening preeclampsia; thrombocytopenia supports both processes.

children.subject: Maternity
children.stem: Complete the sentence. The nurse determines that the priority problem is {1}, and the most immediate goal is to {2}.

choices.text: risk for seizure from severe preeclampsia
prevent eclamptic seizures and lower blood pressure

children.rationale: The severe features place the client at high risk for an eclamptic seizure, so seizure prevention with magnesium sulfate and controlling severe-range blood pressure take priority over less urgent problems.

children.subject: Maternity
children.stem: For each intervention, click to specify whether it is indicated or contraindicated for this client.

rows.text: Place the client in a quiet, low-stimulation room
Administer IV labetalol for severe-range blood pressure
Encourage frequent visitors and bright lighting
Administer ergometrine to reduce bleeding risk

children.rationale: Magnesium sulfate, a low-stimulation environment, and antihypertensives are core preeclampsia care. Stimulation can provoke seizures and ergometrine raises blood pressure, so both are contraindicated.

children.subject: Pharmacology
children.stem: While the magnesium sulfate infusion is running, which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Keep calcium gluconate available at the bedside
Withhold all fetal heart rate monitoring
Encourage the client to ambulate frequently

children.rationale: Magnesium toxicity is detected through loss of reflexes, respiratory depression, and falling urine output, so these are monitored and calcium gluconate is the antidote kept ready. Fetal monitoring continues and ambulation is unsafe.

children.subject: Maternity
children.stem: Which findings indicate the treatment has been effective? Select all that apply.

options.text: Deep tendon reflexes 2+ with adequate respirations
Urine output 60 mL in the past hour
Reappearance of visual spots and epigastric pain

children.rationale: Falling blood pressure, resolving headache and vision changes, preserved reflexes with adequate respirations, and maintained urine output all show the therapy is working. Returning visual and epigastric symptoms would signal worsening disease.
